domain_setting: A pedestrian and driver navigation world linking neighborhood maps, road layouts, compass bearings, directions between landmarks, route planning, and measurement of travel distance.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use a 304x192 stage; keep roads, map markers, and figures inside x=24..280 and y=18..174.
All top-down map scenes use north toward the top edge, with a consistent eight-point compass rose when orientation is needed.
Show directional meaning with a high-contrast blue route arrow and a gold destination marker; avoid lettering and numerals.
Use consistent building silhouettes, intersections, curbs, sidewalks, and map panels so positional relationships are easy to compare.
Street-level scenes use a small adult traveler or car as a scale cue; map scenes show roads as bold paths and landmarks as simple color blocks.
Distance units use measurement bars and route segments without numbers; no readable addresses, street names, map labels, or GPS coordinates.

polysemy_resolution_table.left: The direction opposite right, as confirmed by the position-and-direction group; ignore the Japanese alternate gloss for leave/left as past tense.
polysemy_resolution_table.right: The direction opposite left, not a moral entitlement or correct answer.
polysemy_resolution_table.past: Continue beyond a landmark while following directions, not a time before now.
polysemy_resolution_table.straight: A direct, unbending route or line, not honesty or a body posture.
polysemy_resolution_table.block: A city block enclosed by streets, selected by the roads-and-places group, not a solid cube or obstruction.
polysemy_resolution_table.key: A small physical key used by a traveler to unlock a car or destination door, following the explicit Japanese gloss; not the legend/key of a map.
polysemy_resolution_table.scales (measure): A weighing scale for travel baggage, following the Japanese gloss; not the ratio scale printed on a map.
polysemy_resolution_table.meter / metre: A metric unit of route length, grouped with kilometer and mile; not a parking meter or electrical meter.
polysemy_resolution_table.address: A destination location on a map and its associated envelope/house marker, not an email address.
polysemy_resolution_table.avenue: A broad, tree-lined urban street, not a private driveway.
polysemy_resolution_table.junction: A road junction where routes join or branch, not a general connection or union.
polysemy_resolution_table.shoulder (road): The narrow edge beside a road for emergency stopping, not a body part.
polysemy_resolution_table.hard shoulder: The paved emergency strip beside a motorway/freeway, distinct from the main travel lanes.
polysemy_resolution_table.freeway: A controlled-access, grade-separated, multi-lane road for fast through traffic, not any urban highway.
polysemy_resolution_table.highway: A major intercity public road, shown as a long route outside the city, not specifically an access-controlled freeway.
polysemy_resolution_table.roadmap: A map focused on roads and travel routes, not a metaphorical plan for a project.
polysemy_resolution_table.map / maps: A folded paper map representing a geographic area, not a graph or map legend.
polysemy_resolution_table.street map: A detailed neighborhood map with a street grid and local landmarks, distinct from a broad regional map or a route-focused road map.
polysemy_resolution_table.go past: Travel beyond an unlabeled landmark, rather than go to it or stop at it.
polysemy_resolution_table.go ahead: Continue forward along the route, not permission in a conversation.
polysemy_resolution_table.stop at: Bring a vehicle or traveler to a halt at a particular destination or landmark.
polysemy_resolution_table.turn / turning: Change travel direction along a curved route at a junction, not rotate a knob or turn an object over.
polysemy_resolution_table.here: The location immediately beside the speaker/traveler, shown with a near-field marker.
polysemy_resolution_table.there: A more distant destination marker away from the speaker/traveler.
polysemy_resolution_table.across from: Directly opposite on the other side of a street or open space.
polysemy_resolution_table.opposite: Two destinations facing each other across a gap, in positional contrast with nearby/adjacent locations.
polysemy_resolution_table.between: In the space bounded by two distinct landmarks.
polysemy_resolution_table.ahead: In front along the current direction of travel.
polysemy_resolution_table.behind: At the rear of a landmark or traveler relative to the current forward direction.
polysemy_resolution_table.in front of: On the forward side of a specific landmark, not simply ahead on a route.
polysemy_resolution_table.next to: Immediately beside and close to one landmark.
polysemy_resolution_table.on the corner: At the junction corner where two streets meet, not a building's interior corner.
polysemy_resolution_table.on the left / on the right: Located on the corresponding side of a north-up route or viewpoint.
polysemy_resolution_table.direction: The bearing or orientation of a route, shown with an arrow or compass rose.
polysemy_resolution_table.kilometer / kilometre: A metric unit for measuring a route; show a short measured segment on a map scale without printed digits.
polysemy_resolution_table.mile: An imperial route-distance unit; show a longer measured road segment than the kilometer card without printed digits.
polysemy_resolution_table.gps: A satellite-assisted navigation receiver locating a traveler on a digital route map, not a paper atlas.
polysemy_resolution_table.compass: A handheld magnetic navigation instrument with a free needle, not a compass direction word.
polysemy_resolution_table.take the first left: Follow a route that turns left at the first junction encountered.
polysemy_resolution_table.take the second right: Pass the first junction and turn right at the next one; use two clearly ordered intersections without numerals.
polysemy_resolution_table.crossroads: A four-way crossing of roads, distinguished from a bend or T-junction.
polysemy_resolution_table.intersection: A place where roads cross, viewed as an urban junction with crossing traffic.
polysemy_resolution_table.corner: The turn point where two streets meet, not a room or object corner.
polysemy_resolution_table.footpath: A narrow pedestrian trail through a park or countryside, distinct from a paved sidewalk beside a street.
polysemy_resolution_table.sidewalk: A paved pedestrian walkway parallel to an urban street, separated from vehicle traffic by a curb.
polysemy_resolution_table.crosswalk: A marked zebra crossing for pedestrians across a road.
polysemy_resolution_table.main road: The primary wider route through a neighborhood, contrasted with smaller side streets.
polysemy_resolution_table.one-way street: A road where all vehicles travel in one direction, shown by aligned arrows.
polysemy_resolution_table.pedestrianized street: An urban street closed to cars and used by pedestrians.
polysemy_resolution_table.street: An urban public road with buildings and sidewalks on both sides, not a rural path.
polysemy_resolution_table.traffic light: A three-color intersection control signal, distinct from a car's turn-signal lamp.

sibling_contrasts.compass_directions: All cards share a north-up map and an eight-ray compass rose; only the target bearing and route destination change. East/west may use sunrise/sunset as quiet reinforcing cues.
sibling_contrasts.position_words: Use identical map anchors for across from/opposite, next to/between, in front of/ahead/behind, here/there, and left/right so placement carries the meaning.
sibling_contrasts.route_actions: Go left/right/straight, go past, stop at, turn, take the first left, and take the second right each get a distinct path through one or more junctions.
sibling_contrasts.road_types: Avenue is tree-lined and urban; street has buildings and sidewalks; footpath is narrow and rural; sidewalk parallels a city road; highway is a major intercity route; freeway is multi-lane and controlled access; main road dominates a neighborhood; hard shoulder is the paved emergency edge.
sibling_contrasts.maps_and_tools: Map is broad geographic layout; street map is a dense local grid; roadmap emphasizes a long route; GPS is electronic and satellite-linked; compass is magnetic; kilometer/mile/meter are distance units; scales is the baggage-weighing device; key is a physical travel key.

art_direction: Use clean editorial navigation diagrams with warm paper, dark slate roads, pale sidewalks, sage land, blue route lines, and amber destination markers. Favor top-down maps for spatial terms and simple street-level scenes for road types. Every route and directional symbol must be legible at card size. Keep map text, street names, letters, numerals, coordinates, logos, and labels out of the SVG.
